A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Graph of States (GoS) work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite reformatting and changed pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original medical and distributed-system diagnosis experiments, including accuracy and cost results, ablations, sensitivity analysis, and appendix error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a structured-state-management comparison in Table 2.

M1.justification: The proposed GoS architecture, reasoning focus, causal graph, ReAct interactions, and backtracking/drill-down procedures remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A. Structured-text state management is an added comparison condition, not a modification of full GoS.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same interactive DiagnosisArena task and 150 production incidents, retaining the same medical-case exclusions. Naming Lenovo replaces the anonymized company designation. The added introductory MATH500, AIME2025, and GPQA figures are presented as previously reported performance, not new GoS evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds 'w/ structured state management,' which stores hypotheses, evidence, and support/refute status in structured text without an explicit causal graph. The eight single-agent/multi-agent CoT, ToT, GoT, and FoT comparators in the main experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains GPT-5.1-2025-11-13, case filtering, the 0/1/2 judging scale, medical human evaluation, retrieval limits of three per expert and five for single agents, and three GoS interaction iterations. No separate change to evaluation procedures is documented for the added ablation.

E4.justification: The new Table 2 ablation tests whether structured textual state management can account for the benefits attributed to the causal graph. Existing component-removal ablations, Figure 5 sensitivity analyses, and appendix error analyses and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 8 retains the same five repeated judge assessments of ten medical cases. Neither version changes seed/run reporting, confidence intervals, significance testing, or other uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: The added Table 2 condition reports 18.12% Match, 59.42% Relevant, and $0.15 per case. All existing Table 2 entries, Tables 1 and 3–5, and plotted results remain unchanged; full GoS has no reported performance change.

T1.justification: The task and reasoning-focus definitions in Equations 1–2, graph/state definitions, transition conditions, and Appendix A algorithms retain the same mathematical content. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: a general-purpose abductive framework, explicit graph/state-machine control, improved diagnostic performance, and publicly available code/prompts. The additional ablation supports these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly interprets the structured-text comparison as evidence that generic context management alone does not explain GoS's gains, attributing the remaining advantage to explicit graph relations and hypothesis updates. Appendix B limitations and Appendix D interpretations are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the anonymous code-and-prompts repository address with a named GitHub repository, and Section 4 identifies Lenovo as the incident-data source. These are access/provenance disclosures; the stated restriction on releasing raw incident data and interaction traces remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds LINC, LOGIC-LM, and Aristotle, distinguishing their symbolic answer derivation from GoS's interactive investigation. The introduction adds Lightman and Rein benchmark citations and removes Peirce (1934). The OpsAgent title/year update refers to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited introductory edits, expands related work and the ablation discussion, adds Acknowledgement and Impact Statement sections, and revises affiliations and punctuation. The main narrative, section sequence, and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: ICML-style formatting changes the title/affiliation placement, running headers, spacing, and float placement and sizing. Table 2 gains one row. All ten figure graphics are retained, and the remaining tables preserve their structures.

improvement.justification: The structured-text control strengthens the causal-graph argument beyond v1's graph-removal comparison: it achieves 18.12% Match versus 31.88% for full GoS and 12.32% without the graph. Added neuro-symbolic related work also clarifies positioning. These are useful, bounded improvements while the primary results, method, and documented limitations remain intact.
